blocks.text: ReAct, short for Reason plus Act, interleaves explicit reasoning steps with real external actions, searching a database, calling a calculator, checking a webpage, rather than reasoning purely from what the model already knows internally.

This topic covers the thought, action, observation loop ReAct uses, why pure reasoning alone falls short for tasks needing outside information, and how this technique lays the groundwork for the agent based systems covered later in this course.
1. What ReAct Actually Means

blocks.alt: Building on tree of thoughts, ReAct interleaves reasoning and action in a loop

blocks.text: ReAct combines reasoning, thinking through what to do next, with acting, actually taking an external action and observing its real result, then feeding that real observation back into the next round of reasoning, rather than reasoning in isolation from start to finish.
2. The Thought, Action, Observation Loop

blocks.alt: Thought leads to action, then observation, then another thought, action, and observation

blocks.text: A ReAct trace follows a repeating pattern, a thought about what to do next, an action actually taken, an observation of the real result that action produced, and then another thought informed by that new observation, this loop continues until the task is complete.

code.content:
Thought: I need to find the current population of Japan.
Action: search("population of Japan")
Observation: Japan's population is approximately 123 million as of the latest data.
Thought: I now have the information needed to answer.
Action: finish("Japan's population is approximately 123 million.")

blocks.text: 3. Why Pure Reasoning Alone Sometimes Falls Short

blocks.alt: Pure reasoning alone is compared against reasoning combined with real external actions

blocks.text: Chain of thought, covered in an earlier topic, reasons entirely from what the model already knows internally, for tasks requiring current information, precise calculation, or interaction with an external system, reasoning alone cannot substitute for actually taking a real action and getting a real result back.
4. How an Action Actually Gets Executed

blocks.alt: The model decides on an action like search, an external tool is actually called, and a real result comes back as an observation

blocks.text: When the model reasoning reaches a point where it decides to take an action, an application running the ReAct loop actually executes that action, calling a real search function, a real calculator, or a real API, then passes the genuine result back to the model as the next observation.

blocks.text: 5. ReAct vs Chain of Thought

blocks.alt: Chain of thought reasons only, ReAct combines reasoning with real actions

blocks.text: Chain of thought reasons entirely within the model own generated text, ReAct genuinely steps outside that boundary, incorporating real world information the model could not have known or computed on its own, this is the core structural difference between the two techniques.

blocks.title: This connects the model to genuinely current or precise information
blocks.content: A chain of thought reasoning about a rapidly changing fact, like a current stock price, can only guess based on training data, ReAct actual action step can retrieve a genuinely current answer instead.

blocks.text: 6. ReAct as the Foundation for Agent Based Systems

blocks.alt: The ReAct foundation leads into the Agent Prompting module covered later

blocks.text: This thought, action, observation loop is the foundational pattern behind the agent based systems covered in the later Agent Prompting module of this course, and in much greater depth in the separate AI Agents and Tool Calling course, an agent is essentially a system built around this same core ReAct loop, often with many more available actions.
7. Implementing the Loop in Practice

A real ReAct implementation needs application code that parses the model chosen action from its generated text, executes the corresponding real function, formats the result back as an observation, and feeds the full updated trace back into the next model call, this orchestration is meaningfully more involved than a single prompt call.
8. A Common Failure Mode, Looping on the Same Action

blocks.alt: A model looping on the same action repeatedly is a failure mode worth watching for

blocks.text: A known failure pattern in ReAct systems is the model repeatedly choosing the same action without making genuine progress, searching for the same thing again after already receiving an answer, watching for and detecting this loop is a practical concern when building a real ReAct based system.
9. When ReAct Is the Right Technique

ReAct is the right choice specifically when a task genuinely needs information or capability the model does not already have internally, current facts, precise calculations, interaction with an external system, for tasks fully answerable from the model own existing knowledge, plain chain of thought is simpler and sufficient.
Worked Example

A developer builds a research assistant using chain of thought alone, it confidently states an outdated statistic from its training data when asked about a rapidly changing figure, since it has no way to check for a current value.

Rebuilding the same assistant using ReAct, giving it a real search action it can invoke, the assistant now reasons that it needs current information, actually calls the search action, receives a genuinely current result as an observation, and produces an accurate, up to date answer instead of relying on a stale internal guess.
Common Mistakes

items: Using ReAct for tasks fully answerable from the model existing knowledge, adding unnecessary complexity
Not detecting when a model loops on the same action repeatedly without making real progress
Failing to properly validate or sanitize the real actions the model requests before actually executing them
Confusing ReAct, which takes real external actions, with chain of thought, which reasons purely internally

blocks.text: Practice

Take a question requiring current or precise external information a model would not reliably know from training alone, sketch out what a ReAct thought, action, observation trace would look like for answering it correctly.
Key Takeaway

ReAct interleaves reasoning with real external actions in a thought, action, observation loop, extending beyond what pure reasoning alone can achieve for tasks needing current information or outside capability, and it forms the direct foundation for the agent based systems covered later in this course.
